newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PNG to consider Australian offer on Bougainville.
newsitem.headline: PNG to consider Australian offer on Bougainville.

text.p: Papua New Guinea said on Friday it would consider Australia's offer to broker peace talks with seccessionist Bougainville rebels after at least 12 government troops were killed in fighting on the island this week.

"We have agreed that we will talk about this (offer) within the context of the programme and aid that is available to us," PNG Deputy Prime Minister Chris Haiveta told a news conference after ministerial talks here between the two neighbours.
The PNG response to the offer to host peace talks follows several days of fighting on Bougainville, a resource-rich island 800 km (500 miles) north east of the PNG capital, Port Moresby.
Australian Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer said the talks had established a basis for dialogue on Bougainville.
"PNG knows Australia remains very willing to assist PNG in facilitating the peace process. In the end, this initiative must, of course, come from the PNG side," Downer told reporters.
Australia has offered urgent humanitarian aid for people caught up in the current fighting on Bougainville.

The PNG government said on Thursday it had recaptured a refugee care centre at Kangu Beach in the south of the island after it had been overrun by Bougainville Revolutionary Army (BRA) rebels. Some 70,000 Bougainvilleans have left their villages to live in the government-controlled care centres.
About 40 soldiers attacked the centre on Wednesday night, meeting heavy resistance from about 120 Bougainville Revolutionary Army (BRA) rebels.
PNG Defence Force chief of staff Colonel Jack Taut earlier told Reuters that 24 rebels belonging to the Bougainville Revolutionary Army had been killed in the operation.
The rebels, who control the island's central region, said two government soldiers were killed in the renewed fighting on Wednesday.

"The Kangu beach was filled with the stench from rotting bodies of the PNG Defence Force soldiers killed since Sunday," the unofficial Bougainville Interim Government said in a statement received here.

The Kangu Beach death toll was the worst since the rebellion began eight years ago. PNG Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan has described the rebel attack as barbaric and a major setback to peace on Bougainville.
The rebels claimed 13 soldiers were killed and five captured when they captured the care centre on Sunday.
Chan said 12 soldiers had been reported killed in the initial battle.

Relations between PNG and Australia have been strained over the eight-year secessionist conflict on Bougainville, particularly over the use of Australian supplied helicopters by government forces in the conflict.
In July, Downer called for the use of the helicopters to be limited to transport and medical evacuations, a move criticised by PNG.
However, both sides played down the dispute on Friday.
Downer said he was confident there would be full adherence to such stipulations in the defence cooperation agreement and Haiveta described the issue as "water under the bridge".
